subject: physics
question_text: Write the force law for simple harmonic motion. What does the negative sign in it mean?

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The force law
lines: For a body in simple harmonic motion the
restoring force is proportional to the

lines.text: F = −k y,   where k = m ω²

steps.why: This one line is the definition of SHM written as a force instead of as an acceleration.
common_mistakes: Writing F = −k v, using velocity instead of displacement.

recall.must_convey: That F equals minus k y, with k equal to m omega squared.
reject: it points back to the mean position

steps.label: The negative sign

lines.text: F and y always point opposite ways

lines: The force pushes the body back towards the
mean position, whichever side it is on.
Without the minus sign the body would be
driven further out and would never oscillate.
steps.why: The minus sign is not decoration — it is the whole reason the motion turns around instead of running away.
common_mistakes: Reading the minus sign as "the force is negative", when it only means the force is opposite to y.

recall.must_convey: That the minus sign means the force is always opposite to the displacement, pushing the body back to the mean position.
accept: pushes it back to the mean position
